title: File DE franchise tax
summary: File the annual Delaware franchise tax and annual report.

parts.title: Calculate franchise tax
parts.guidance: Confirm the Delaware entity type and year. For a corporation, reconcile authorized and issued shares, par values, gross assets and relevant charter changes to the records. Compare applicable calculation methods using current Division of Corporations instructions, resolving unusual cases with the tax adviser. Preserve the inputs and calculation so the selected amount can be explained and checked against the filing service.

parts.title: Gather officer and director info
parts.guidance: Collect the officer, director, business-address and other details requested for this corporation’s annual report. Compare appointments and addresses with the prior report and resolve changes or conflicting records. Check which information will become public before entering personal details. Use the verified current information when preparing the report’s certification.

parts.title: File on Delaware portal
parts.guidance: Identify the corporation and reporting year in the official Delaware service using its verified file number. Enter the report details and reconcile the displayed tax with the reviewed calculation. Complete the declaration and submission through the company’s authorized filing route. Save the submitted report and check whether payment is included or outstanding. Resolve portal errors before treating the filing as complete.

verify.how: The Delaware portal returns a filing confirmation and the annual report shows filed for the tax year.

parts.title: Pay franchise tax
parts.guidance: Match the tax, report fee, adjustments and prior payments to the state account and reviewed calculation. Verify the entity, period and funding account through the company’s payment-approval process, then submit the payment and check settlement. If filing already collected the amount, reconcile that receipt before paying again. Resolve unexplained balances with the tax adviser or state.

verify.how: A payment confirmation number is issued and the entity stays in Good Standing in the Delaware entity search.

cost.note: Minimum: $175 minimum franchise tax (authorized-shares method) plus the $50 annual report filing fee; the assumed-par-value method minimum is $400 plus the $50 fee. Scales with authorized shares.

parts.title: Save confirmation receipt
parts.guidance: Save the annual report, calculation, payment receipt and state acknowledgement under the correct year and entity. Reconcile transaction references and amounts to the ledger. Keep pending confirmations or unexplained balances visible, and update the compliance calendar from the verified filing status and next requirement.

parts.title: Pay the California minimum franchise tax ($800, FTB)
parts.guidance: Assess the corporation’s California facts, tax year and treatment with the tax adviser, including minimum-tax applicability and first-year or other exceptions. Reconcile income-based tax and prior payments separately from the catalog’s stated minimum. Submit any resulting payment through the company’s authorized tax-payment route and retain the calculation and receipt. The California obligation must be established for this company before paying.

references.title: FTB — C corporations (the $800 minimum franchise tax)

metadata.supportReason: Delaware franchise tax portal has no API. System calculates the tax, pre-fills data, provides step-by-step guidance.

geoNotes.summary: No franchise tax; the keep-the-company-alive annual ritual is the MCA pair — financial statements (AOC-4) and the annual return (MGT-7/MGT-7A) — filed on MCA V3 (fronted by NSWS; mca.gov.in blocks automated access), with per-day late fees that compound fast.

The closest analog is the confirmation statement: an annual Companies House filing (£34 online) confirming registered details — the same keep-the-company-in-good-standing ritual, but with no tax attached.

No franchise tax; the closest mandatory annual levy is the IHK-Beitrag — every trading company is automatically a chamber-of-commerce member and pays a small revenue-based contribution each year, no filing ritual attached.

The closest analog is the CFE: an annual local business levy assessed per commune on every company (with a first-year exemption), paid through the espace professionnel — France's version of 'you pay something every year just for existing'.

No franchise tax; the keep-the-company-current annual ritual is the IES — one electronic declaration that files the accounts to the registry, the tax annexes to AT and the statistics to INE in a single submission.

No franchise tax; the analog is the Corporations Canada annual return — a small online filing due within 60 days of the incorporation anniversary (it is not a tax return), and missing it can lead to administrative dissolution.
